mechanism_narrative: The Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) level is a consistent positive leading indicator for S&P 500 5-day forward returns, with historical data showing positive returns in all periods where FEDFUNDS is observed, regardless of its value. The signal is always active and predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the 5-day periods following FEDFUNDS observations, as measured by a 3-year rolling window of historical data.

mechanism_narrative: A Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) level below 2.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which compresses discount rates and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS <= 2.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS <= 2.5%) and strong labor market (PAYEMS > 150,000) indicates accommodative monetary policy coupled with robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns through reduced discount rates and elevated corporate earnings.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong labor market
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where both FEDFUNDS <= 2.5% and PAYEMS > 150,000 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, where the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) rises by more than 0.5 percentage points over three months, the resulting increase in discount rates and reduced liquidity leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% in 3 months over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 thousand units indicate strong consumer demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of broader economic activity and positive equity returns, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where HOUST > 1200 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 110 indicates robust manufacturing output, which signals strong supply capacity and positive economic momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO > 110 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% indicates a tight labor market, which is associated with strong wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE < 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) level above 250 indicates moderate inflation, which reflects stable economic conditions without deflationary pressures, resulting in positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 250 over a 3-year rolling window.
